\chapter{Mock exam}\label{ch:mock-exam}

\emph{Can you pass the theory paper today?} This paper follows the format of the Level 1 theory exam: multiple-choice questions of one mark each, two hours, and no negative marking. Answer every question, then check yourself with the key at the end. Each question comes from a chapter of this book, so a wrong answer points to the chapter to revise.

\section*{Introduction to yoga and yogic practices}
\begin{enumerate}[series=mock]
\item\label{mq:1} From which Sanskrit root does the word yoga come?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
\item yam
\item yaj
\item yuga
\item yuj
\end{enumerate}
\item\label{mq:2} Which three senses did Panini give for the root yuj?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
\item Breath, posture and diet
\item Body, mind and spirit
\item Action, devotion and knowledge
\item Union, concentration (samadhi) and control
\end{enumerate}
\item\label{mq:3} Which text defines yoga as skill in action?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
\item The Yoga Sutra
\item The Hatha Pradipika
\item The Bhagavad Gita
\item The Gheranda Samhita
\end{enumerate}
\item\label{mq:4} Which text calls yoga a skilful means of calming the mind?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
\item The Hatha Pradipika
\item The Narada Bhakti Sutra
\item The Brahma Sutras
\item The Yoga Vasishtha
\end{enumerate}
\item\label{mq:5} In yogic lore, who is the first yogi (Adiyogi) and the first teacher (Adi Guru)?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
\item Patanjali
\item Svatmarama
\item Vyasa
\item Shiva
\end{enumerate}
\item\label{mq:6} Which period of yoga's history is marked by the hatha yoga texts?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
\item The Vedic period
\item The pre-classical period
\item The post-classical period
\item The classical period
\end{enumerate}
\item\label{mq:7} Which of these is a nastika school?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
\item Nyaya
\item Samkhya
\item Mimamsa
\item Charvaka
\end{enumerate}
\item\label{mq:8} Which two principles does Samkhya teach?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
\item Prana and apana
\item Ida and pingala
\item Sattva and tamas
\item Purusha and prakriti
\end{enumerate}
\item\label{mq:9} How long should a practitioner wait after practice before a bath or a meal?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
\item No wait is needed
\item About 5 minutes
\item About 20 to 30 minutes
\item About three hours
\end{enumerate}
\item\label{mq:10} How does a yoga session begin?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
\item With a prayer or invocation
\item With kapalabhati
\item With shavasana
\item With surya namaskara
\end{enumerate}
\item\label{mq:11} Which are the three gunas?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
\item Vata, pitta and kapha
\item Manas, buddhi and chitta
\item Ida, pingala and sushumna
\item Sattva, rajas and tamas
\end{enumerate}
\item\label{mq:12} Which are the four parts of the inner instrument (antahkarana)?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
\item Manas, buddhi, chitta, ahamkara
\item Prana, apana, samana, vyana
\item Sattva, rajas, tamas, prakriti
\item Annamaya, pranamaya, manomaya, anandamaya
\end{enumerate}
\item\label{mq:13} On which sheath (kosha) does pranayama mainly work?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
\item Annamaya
\item Manomaya
\item Pranamaya
\item Anandamaya
\end{enumerate}
\item\label{mq:14} Which is the correct order of the five great elements?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
\item Earth, water, fire, air, space
\item Water, earth, air, fire, space

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]

\item Udana

\item Samana

\section*{Yoga texts}
\begin{enumerate}[resume*=mock]
\item\label{mq:21} Which list gives the five movements of the mind (vrittis) in the Yoga Sutra?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
\item Right knowledge, error, imagination, sleep and memory
\item Desire, anger, greed, pride and envy
\item Seeing, hearing, touching, tasting and smelling
\item Waking, dreaming, sleep, trance and death
\end{enumerate}
\item\label{mq:22} Which two means does the Yoga Sutra give for stilling the movements of the mind?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
\item Asana and pranayama
\item Japa and kirtana
\item Abhyasa and vairagya
\item Dhauti and neti
\end{enumerate}
\item\label{mq:23} Which are the two definitions of yoga in the second chapter of the Gita?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
\item Stilling of the mind and union with God
\item Evenness of mind in success and failure, and skill in action
\item Control of breath and control of the senses
\item Renunciation and devotion
\end{enumerate}
\item\label{mq:24} Who wrote the Hatha Pradipika?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]

\item Gheranda
\item Svatmarama
\item Vyasa
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
\item Four
\item Six
\item Seven
\item Eighteen
\end{enumerate}
\item\label{mq:26} What is the yoga of the Gheranda Samhita called?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
\item Eight-limbed yoga
\item Seven-limbed yoga

\item Four-limbed yoga
\end{enumerate}

\item Twelve asanas and five mudras
\end{enumerate}
\item\label{mq:28} Which three make up the Prasthanatrayi?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
\item The Upanishads, the Brahma Sutras and the Bhagavad Gita

\item The Yoga Sutra, the Hatha Pradipika and the Gheranda Samhita
\item The Ramayana, the Mahabharata and the Puranas
\end{enumerate}
\item\label{mq:29} What does mitahara mean?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
\item Fasting
\item Measured, wholesome food
\item Raw food only
\item One meal a day
\end{enumerate}
\item\label{mq:30} Which text gives the idea of yuktahara?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
\item The Bhagavad Gita
\item The Yoga Sutra
\item The Gheranda Samhita
\item The Brahma Sutras
\end{enumerate}
\item\label{mq:31} Which Gita verse speaks of moderation in eating, recreation, effort, sleep and waking?

\item Chapter six, verse seventeen
\item Chapter twelve, verse thirteen
\item Chapter eighteen, verse sixty-six
\end{enumerate}
\item\label{mq:32} Which Gita chapter lists the divine qualities?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
\item Chapter two
\item Chapter six
\item Chapter sixteen
\item Chapter eighteen
\end{enumerate}
\item\label{mq:33} In the second chapter of the Gita, which chain of thought leads to anger?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
\item Desire, attachment, dwelling on sense objects, anger
\item Dwelling on sense objects, attachment, desire, anger
\item Fear, greed, attachment, anger
\item Ignorance, pride, envy, anger
\end{enumerate}
\item\label{mq:34} Which of these is not one of the five kleshas?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
\item Ignorance (avidya)
\item Ego-sense (asmita)
\item Liking (raga)
\item Non-attachment (vairagya)
\end{enumerate}
\item\label{mq:35} What is pratipaksha bhavana?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]

\item Replacing a negative thought with its positive opposite
\item Gazing at a candle flame
\item Repeating a mantra
\end{enumerate}
\item\label{mq:36} Which are the inner limbs (antaranga) of Patanjala yoga?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
\item Yama, niyama and asana
\item Asana, pranayama and pratyahara
\item Dharana, dhyana and samadhi
\item Pranayama, dharana and dhyana
\end{enumerate}
\item\label{mq:37} Which limb comes fifth in Patanjali's eight limbs?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
\item Pranayama
\item Pratyahara
\item Dharana
\item Asana
\end{enumerate}
\item\label{mq:38} What does eka-tattva abhyasa mean?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
\item Practice on one principle, to steady a scattered mind
\item Practice of one asana a day
\item Practice alone, without a teacher
\item Practice once a week
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
